body:
### Is this a reproducible bug?

- [x] I confirm this is a reproducible bug, not a feature request, idea, question, contribution proposal, or direction check.

### Current behavior

Any CLI that stores credentials in the macOS login keychain fails inside herdr panes, while the identical command works in a plain terminal on the same machine.

Observable difference from inside any herdr pane:

- `launchctl managername` prints `Background` (a plain terminal prints `Aqua`)
- `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` fails with `User interaction is not allowed.` (succeeds in a plain terminal)

Concrete casualty: a Google CLI with keychain-stored OAuth tokens reports "Secret not found in keyring" in every herdr pane, works fine outside. Took me a while to figure out why the same tool behaved differently in two terminals side by side.

### Expected behavior

A shell inside a herdr pane has the same login-session context as a plain terminal, keychain access included. tmux panes on the same machine pass both checks above (`Aqua`, keychain readable), so this is the behavior I expected from a terminal multiplexer on macOS.

### Reproduction

1. plain terminal: `launchctl managername` -> `Aqua`; `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` -> prints keychain settings
2. `herdr`, open any pane, run the same two commands -> `Background` and `User interaction is not allowed.`
3. any keychain-backed CLI now fails to read its stored credential inside the pane and works outside it

### Impact

Every keychain-backed credential helper breaks inside herdr panes - hit me through Google CLI tooling in an agent fleet, and the only workarounds are per-tool file-based token stores, which trade away at-rest security. It also produces confusing split-brain situations where a credential works in one terminal and not another.

### Environment

- Herdr version: 0.7.1
- Update channel (stable or preview): stable
- Operating system: macOS 26.5.1 (Apple Silicon, M4 Pro Mac mini)
- Terminal: WezTerm
- Shell, if relevant: zsh
- Relevant config, if any: config.toml managed via nix/home-manager

comments.body:
i tried to reproduce this on my mac, but both a normal terminal and a normal herdr pane report `Aqua`, and `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` succeeds in both.

could you share a bit more process/install context?

```sh
command -v herdr
herdr --version
pgrep -af 'herdr( server)?'
herdr status server --json
```

also, inside the affected herdr pane:

```sh
launchctl managername
security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
echo $?
```

and in the plain terminal that works:

```sh
launchctl managername
security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
echo $?
```

the key thing i want to pin down is how the existing `herdr server` was first started, since this looks launch-context dependent.

good hunch - it is launch-context dependent, and i can confirm the mechanism end to end now. i can also rule out the install method: my herdr is nix-managed, but it's your own release binary fetched verbatim (no patching), and the same binary behaves perfectly once the server sits in the right launchd domain.

setup: herdr 0.7.1, upstream release binary on nix (`command -v herdr` -> `/etc/profiles/per-user/kunchen/bin/herdr`), macOS 26.5, M4 Pro mac mini.

what happened here: my long-lived `herdr server` had not been started from a GUI terminal - and once a server is in a Background session it self-perpetuates, because restarting it from inside one of its own panes inherits Background again. in that state, from any pane, `launchctl managername` printed `Background` and `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` failed with "User interaction is not allowed", while a plain terminal printed `Aqua` and succeeded.

the confirmation: i moved the server to a per-user LaunchAgent registered in the gui domain (`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/<label>`). same binary, same config - now `launchctl managername` inside every pane prints `Aqua` (re-verified just now) and keychain-backed CLIs work.

caveat: i can't produce the failing outputs live anymore without tearing down a working fleet - the Background-state outputs are from my notes at the time.

repro suggestion: start the server from any non-Aqua context (e.g. via `ssh localhost`, or a Background launchd job), then open panes and check `launchctl managername`.

suggestion: document this and ship a LaunchAgent template for the gui domain (what i did), or have the daemonize path register in the uid's gui domain when one exists.

thanks for digging into this. that confirms this is launch-context dependent rather than install-method dependent.

i’m going to treat this as an edge case / expected macos behavior for now: if the long-lived `herdr server` is started from a `Background` launchd context, panes inherit that context, and keychain-backed tools can fail. preventing this automatically would mean adding explicit macos launch-agent/gui-domain management commands, plus lifecycle docs and failure handling, which is more product surface than i want to take on right now.

the practical fix is to start the server from a gui terminal or from a per-user launchagent in `gui/$UID`, as you did. i’m closing this, but leaving the issue here because your notes are useful for anyone searching the issue board later.

thanks again for the report and for confirming the mechanism.
can we add this to troubleshooting? got hit by this myself. not sure where the server started because I always start it from ghostty, but once stop and restarted, it works

title: macOS: panes run in a Background launchd session, so keychain-backed CLIs fail inside herdr
